card.title: The table that predicted the future

panels.text: 1869. Dmitri Mendeleev arranges the elements by atomic mass and sees that their chemical properties follow a pattern.
Not every element was known, so his table had gaps. Instead of hiding them, he predicted that undiscovered elements would fill them.
He called one eka-aluminium, expecting an atomic mass of about 68 and a density of about 6.0 g/cm³. In 1875 Lecoq de Boisbaudran discovered gallium.
Gallium came out at about 69.7 and 5.91 g/cm³. In 1886 germanium, predicted as eka-silicon, matched too. The table was not just a list, it was a map with blanks.

probes.question: What did Mendeleev do with the gaps in his table?
options: Left them blank because the data was missing
Predicted that undiscovered elements would fill them
Filled them with copies of nearby elements

probes.question: True or false: gallium, discovered in 1875, closely matched Mendeleev's predicted eka-aluminium.

claims.claim: In 1869 Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic mass and chemical properties followed a pattern
claims.quote: The first periodic table to become generally accepted was that of the Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869; he formulated the periodic law as a dependence of chemical properties on atomic mass .

claims.claim: His table had gaps and he predicted undiscovered elements would fill them (probe 1 answer)
claims.quote: he noted gaps in the table and predicted that then-unknown elements existed with properties appropriate to fill those gaps.
He named them eka-boron, eka-aluminium, eka-silicon, and eka-manganese, with respective atomic masses of 44, 68, 72, and 100.

claims.claim: Gallium discovered 1875 by Lecoq de Boisbaudran (also probe 2)
claims.quote: which was discovered, soon after Mendeleev predicted its existence, in 1875 by Paul Emile Lecoq de Boisbaudran .

claims.claim: Predicted density 6.0 g/cm3 vs gallium 5.91; mass 68 vs about 69.7 (page 69.723)
In 1886 germanium, predicted as eka-silicon, matched too
claims.quote: germanium was called eka-silicon until its discovery in 1886

claims.claim: Eka-silicon proved a good predictor of germanium
claims.quote: proved to be good predictors of the properties of scandium (Sc, 21), gallium (Ga, 31), technetium (Tc, 43), and germanium (Ge, 32) respectively
